summary: Laurent Van Cutsem specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees from Université libre de Bruxelles, KU Leuven, and Ghent University (Doctor, 2023), where he served as Doctor-Assistant from 2023 to 2026.

Laurentios Myriantheus worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Rizarios Ecclesiastical School and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Munich, studying under Martin Haug and Wilhelm von Christ.

Laurie L. Patton is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and the University of Chicago (PhD, 1991). She held professorships at Emory and Duke, and served as president of Middlebury College (2015–2024).
Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. As attested in 2026, she pursued Ph.D. studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence Cohen is an Indology scholar who earned a Doctor of Pharmacy from the University of Southern California (1979). His academic career includes appointments at Washington State University, UNT Health Science Center, and UC Berkeley.

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He served as a director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a professor of theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Epstein is a Tibetologist who earned a BS from UCLA and an MD from George Washington University, followed by medical training. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Washington from circa 1987 to 2004.

Lawrence Heyworth Mills was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at NYU, Virginia Theological Seminary, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Oxford (M.A., 1888), where he became a professor in 1897.
Lawrence J. McCrea is an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. Attested as a professor at Cornell University in 2026, he has taught Whitney Cox and James McHugh.

Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at several institutions, including Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, and St. John's College, and received a doctorate from the California Institute of Integral Studies.
Laxmanshastri Joshi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati from circa 1916 to 1923 and later served as director of Prajna Pathashala from circa 1955 to 1994.
Laxmidhar Behera works in computational studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at IIT Kanpur and IIT Mandi, and he taught Jivnesh Sandhan.

Lazăr Șăineanu was a linguist who studied at Bucharest under Georgian and Haşdeu, in Paris, and at Leipzig under Brugmann and Leskien (Ph.D., 1889). From 1890 to 1892, he acted for Haşdeu at the University of Bucharest.
LeRoy Carr Barret was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (1894–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

LeRoy Carr Barrett was an Indologist who studied at Washington and Lee and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He taught at Johns Hopkins, Princeton, and Dartmouth before becoming professor of Latin at Trinity College in 1910.

Leah Judith Zahler was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Geshe Wangyal, Harvey B. Aronson, and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Lee Jonathan Chilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tasmania, Macquarie University, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the University of Sydney, where he completed an MPhil in 2024.

Lee Ling Ting is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Adelaide (BA), Peking University (MA), and Harvard University (PhD), Ting became a postdoctoral fellow at Vassar College in 2024.
Lee Yearley is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He held a professorship at Stanford University (attested 1989–1992), where he later became emeritus (attested 2026).

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2011, he served as professor emeritus of anthropology at Drew University and as a research associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.
